What part of Legal Immigration Don't You Understand?

That it is a long and complicated track to follow. It takes a long time (6-20 years) even if you are eligible.

Of the three immigrants I know with a US citizen spouse:

  • One was sent back to Scotland separating her from her husband and child. She was eventually able to get reunited with her family.

  • Another waited years to find her paper work had been shredded by government worker. She got a lawyer and narrowly avoided deportation to Brazil.

  • The last had his immigration paper work denied and he was ordered back to Bangladesh. Even though he was married to a US citizen and working at a job.

Seems like a pretty reasonable system. Relatives of citizens can get in, relatives of non-citizens can get in only if they are close relatives (spouses, dependent children). Skilled workers who have a job offer can get in. And, you must be here for the long haul before becoming a citizen.

Is there any reason we'd want random people with no family, no job, no skills to attain a job to enter the country? What would they do what once they got here?
